newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans activists chained to "nuclear" freighter.
newsitem.headline: Germans activists chained to "nuclear" freighter.

text.p: Anti-nuclear activists chained themselves to the rope of a freighter carrying nuclear fuel while it was anchored in a German port, a spokesman for Greenpeace environmental group said on Saturday.

The overnight protest action was to highlight the potential dangers of transporting nuclear materials, the spokesman said. It came days after a train carrying nuclear waste derailed in France sparking renewed fears about nuclear transportation.
Police in the port of Bremerhaven ended the blockade early on Saturday morning and the freighter set off for Dounreay nuclear processing centre in northern Britain.
Ten Greenpeace activists were detained briefly.
Greenpeace said the freighter was carrying 83 kilogrammes of nuclear fuel including uranium and highly-enriched plutonium which they said was enough to build a nuclear bomb.

The German train carrying nuclear waste, which derailed in eastern France on Tuesday, was put back on the tracks the following day. French and German officials said there had been no leakage of radiation and no danger to the public.
But environmental groups across Germany reacted with horror at the news, saying it proved what they had always said -- that nuclear waste transportation was potentially lethal and should be stopped.
